<description>
While looking into #36759 I discovered `-notorcontrol` did the opposite of what would be expected from it and I then checked for similar issues in other init options. There are several more where `-nofoo` does something surprising including one of them crashing the node.

This PR attempts to fix all these surprising behaviors while also keeping things as simple as possible and just change behavior to something that makes sense harmless in the context of the option. Fixes that use a common approach for the fix are grouped together into a commit even if the options included themselves may have no relation at all.

| Commit | Problematic options behavior | Fix approach |
|---|---|---|
| [mempool: Reject cluster limits below 1](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/512773d111daaa4330c873ed5889b9ef511f6e3a) | `-nolimitclustercount` hits an assertion in `TxGraph` on the first mempool transaction. `-nolimitclustersize` rejects every transaction. | Reject values below 1 at startup. |
| [args: Add NEGATE_TO_EMPTY so -nofoo reads as an empty string](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/ac4b8feb3fe151d1b00085cfe15a856ccede6e6e) | `GetArg()` returns `"0"` for a negated option. The `-no*notify` options run the command `0`, `-nosigner` uses `0` as signer, `-noi2psam` fails startup and `-norpcpassword` sets the password to `0`. Opt-in because options like `-noonion` and `-noblockfilterindex` depend on reading `"0"`. | New opt-in flag `NEGATE_TO_EMPTY` makes `GetArg()` return `""`. |
| [init: Read -cjdnsreachable and -help as booleans](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/dc4ddbacf791ac6742261bf66dcf42887bfb74ff) | `-cjdnsreachable=0` and `-nocjdnsreachable` turn CJDNS on. `-nohelp` prints the help. | Use `GetBoolArg()` instead of `IsArgSet()`. |
| [args, wallet: Fix empty and negated -blocksdir and -walletdir](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/be71581c2fc65722f6e335e6506cda342eb23ef7) | `-noblocksdir` writes block files relative to the working directory. `-nowalletdir` fails startup. | Fail at startup with `DISALLOW_NEGATION`. An empty value falls back to the default directory, like `-datadir` does. |
| [init: Require -nolistenonion with -notorcontrol](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/44b1c5b05057bf3a768eac63922c085163975dcc) | `-notorcontrol` connects to `0.0.0.0:9051`, which reaches a local Tor. | Fail at startup unless `-listenonion` is disabled. |
| [init: Disallow negating options where it has no meaning](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/6447b07919072f12aba36313814fd4962dd4363a) | `-nocheckblocks`, `-nomaxreceivebuffer`, `-nomaxsendbuffer` and `-nomaxtipage` read as 0, the opposite of what the user asked for. | Fail at startup with `DISALLOW_NEGATION`. |

`-nomempoolexpiry` has a similar kind of problem. It evicts transactions as soon as the next one arrives. I left it out because #36540 already is open and addresses this.
</description>

[2026-11-24] rc:4682939306 inline on src/init.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-24):
In commit "init: Require -nolistenonion with -notorcontrol" (c0bc030a10d7aaea62ea22ce6cabe875ac111eaa)

Not blocking, but it might be worth adding a short release note, since some settings that used to be accepted now fail at startup: `-notorcontrol` while onion listening is enabled, `-noblocksdir`, `-nocheckblocks`, `-nomaxreceivebuffer`, `-nomaxsendbuffer` and `-nomaxtipage`. A note listing them, with `-nolistenonion` as the replacement for `-notorcontrol`, would help anyone who hits the new errors after upgrading. The [Ralph review](https://review.fish.foo/report/36880-8731550b059b76bbecadae87f28638ef706b57c7-2836-3.html#finding-finding%3A2) suggested this too.
[2026-11-24] rc:4683289347 inline on src/init.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-24):
In commit "init: Require -nolistenonion with -notorcontrol" (c0bc030a10d7aaea62ea22ce6cabe875ac111eaa)

I think an error explaining how these are connected could be more helpful here:

```suggestion
        return InitError(Untranslated("-notorcontrol cannot be used while -listenonion is enabled (the default). Use -nolistenonion to stop connecting to the Tor control port."));
```

`-listenonion` is on by default, so someone passing `-notorcontrol` may not know how it's involved. And `-nolistenonion` on its own is enough to stop the node from connecting to the control port, since [`-listenonion`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/8731550b059b76bbecadae87f28638ef706b57c7/src/init.cpp#L2314-L2320) is the only thing that uses it.
[2026-11-24] rc:4683301185 inline on src/common/args.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-24):
In commit "args, wallet: Fix empty and negated -blocksdir and -walletdir" (e954bebe3591d0d3fd79648e729a87fd532a0fce)

I think the commit message could be clearer about what changes, and the description of the old `-noblocksdir` behavior only applies to some platforms. When I ran a master build on Linux, `-noblocksdir` and `-blocksdir=` didn't write blocks to the working directory. Startup aborted with an uncaught exception ("filesystem error: cannot make absolute path"), because `fs::absolute("")` throws with libstdc++ and only returns the working directory with libc++. Here's a suggestion listing the before and after behavior for each value that changes:

```text
args, wallet: Reject -noblocksdir/-nowalletdir and treat empty values as unset

This changes the behavior of negated and empty -blocksdir and -walletdir
values. Other values behave the same as before.

-noblocksdir
  Before: same as -blocksdir= below.
  After: startup error "Negating of -blocksdir is meaningless and
  therefore forbidden".

-blocksdir=
  Before: depended on the C++ standard library. With libstdc++ (most
  Linux builds), startup aborted with an uncaught "cannot make absolute
  path" filesystem exception. With libc++ (macOS), block files were
  written under the working directory while the block index stayed in
  the datadir.
  After: blocks are stored in the default location in the datadir, as if
  -blocksdir were not set.

-nowalletdir
  Before: startup error 'Specified -walletdir "" does not exist'.
  After: startup error "Negating of -walletdir is meaningless and
  therefore forbidden".

-walletdir=
  Before: startup error 'Specified -walletdir "" does not exist'.
  After: wallets are loaded from the default wallet directory, as if
  -walletdir were not set.

The negated forms are rejected, like -nodatadir, instead of falling back
to the default directory, because -noblocksdir and -nowalletdir read as
not using a directory at all.
```

The `-noblocksdir` row in the PR description table could be updated the same way.

This only checks that the node starts with `-noi2psam -norpcpassword`, so most options changed in this commit have no test showing that `-nofoo` now does something sensible. I tried adding a check for each one to the existing functional test for that option. Each passes `-foo=X -nofoo`, the way someone would turn off a setting from `bitcoin.conf`:

- `feature_startupnotify.py`: `-nostartupnotify` doesn't run the command.
- `feature_notifications.py`: `-noblocknotify` and `-nowalletnotify` write no notification files and run no command. `-noalertnotify` only checks that no command runs, since the alert doesn't fire again after a restart.
- `rpc_signer.py`: with `-nosigner`, `enumeratesigners` reports that no signer is configured.
- `p2p_i2p_ports.py`: with `-noi2psam`, I2P is unreachable and has no proxy.
- `rpc_users.py`: `-norpcpassword` falls back to cookie authentication, and `-norpcuser` sets an empty user name, not `0`.
- `interface_bitcoin_cli.py`: `bitcoin-cli -norpcpassword` uses the cookie file. `-norpcuser` sends an empty user name, which this node can't distinguish from `0` since it uses cookie authentication.
- `feature_torcontrol.py`: with `-notorpassword`, the node uses NULL authentication.

All of these pass on this branch and fail with the `NEGATE_TO_EMPTY` check in `GetArg()` commented out. With the old behavior, the notify options print "0: command not found" to stderr, which the test framework checks when stopping the node. With these tests, the startup check here could probably be dropped. Feel free to use any of this:
